title: The same work contracted out again, for the long term, with no plan to bring it back
question: How often is a request a repeat of work already contracted out, and how often does the department say the need is permanent?
finding: 289 requests say the work was contracted out before (in the last three years, or under an earlier approval). Of 301 newer forms that answer Q5, 241 call the need long-term rather than temporary; of 241 that answer Q5f, 209 say there is no plan to transition the work back to City staff.
how: Newer forms: “Has your department contracted out these services in the last three years?”, “How many contracts?”, Q5 (temporary or long-term) and Q5f (plan to transition the work back). Older forms: question 1C, “Has this service been provided in the past?”, where it cites an earlier approval.
limits: Repeat and long-term contracting is common for software support, construction management and services the City has never staffed; the Commission approves it. Long-term contracting for work City classes perform is the question the Charter’s rule on personal-services contracts exists to ask, and the answer needs the cost of each option.
